title: Tech Note: Sign a 4D App Package using SignTool on Windows
author: Karim Meghraoui, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: Code signing itself remains essential for Windows deployment, but the specific mechanics have moved on: Microsoft has deprecated SHA1 for code signing (SHA256 is now mandatory), and self-signed certificates like the one generated here are not trusted by Windows SmartScreen/antivirus for public distribution — a properly issued certificate from a trusted CA (or an EV certificate) is required in practice today. The SignTool command-line tool itself is still the correct/current tool.
related_updates: SHA1 signing is deprecated/no longer trusted by modern Windows and browsers; SHA256 (or newer) is now required
Self-signed certificates as shown are suitable only for testing, not real-world distribution which requires a CA-issued (ideally EV) code-signing certificate
SignTool remains the current, standard Windows code-signing utility
